newsitem.title: RWANDA: Zaire refugees say they left many dead, wounded.
newsitem.headline: Zaire refugees say they left many dead, wounded.

text.p: Zairean refugees who fled war in eastern Zaire said on Monday they had left behind many dead and dying in huts just across the border.
U.N. officials say about 3,300 Zaireans and 700 Rwandans crossed into Rwanda from Zaire on Sunday.
Refugees told Reuters at Mutura border crossing into western Rwanda that fighting erupted a week ago pitting Zairean soldiers and Rwanda Hutu militiamen against attackers thought to be Tutsi rebels.

They said it broke into full-scale war on Saturday with most of the firing on Kibumba refugee camp coming from across the nearby Rwandan border as well as from the direction of an ethnic Tutsi area to the north.

"Our settlement including the Rwandan refugee camp of Kibumba was first attacked last Monday," said Banze Kunyurwa, a father of five, who said in tears he suffered at the hands of Zairean troops who had looted his house and raped his wife.
"The fighting continued intermittently until Saturday when it became a full-scale war," he added, speaking in Swahili.
The Zairean refugees, who lived in a village near Kibumba refugee camp, said they suspected ethnic Tutsi rebels from the Masisi region were responsible for the attack.

"Many of our own people and the Rwandans were killed. I cannot tell you how many but there are a lot of dead bodies in the huts you see," he said pointing to Kibumba and his settlement five km (three miles) west of Mutura border point.
"There are also a lot of wounded in those houses but there is no one to bring them out to Rwanda," Kunyurwa said.

As he spoke, watched by Rwandan soldiers, machinegun fire rang out on the Zairean side of the border. Aid workers said the Kibumba zone was still contested by the Tutsi rebels and former Rwandan Hutu army soldiers, who fled from Rwanda in 1994.

Across a hill from Mutura, Kibumba camp was clearly visible and looked virtually empty. A few small pillars of smoke were visible and gunshots intermittently rang out from the camp, which had some 200,000 residents until they fled at the weekend.

Aid workers with Medecins Sans Frontieres-Belgium (MSF- Doctors Without Borders) on the Rwandan side of the border said they had treated seven Zaireans with gunshot wounds on Sunday and three more were brought in on Monday in serious condition.
"We are told by the refugees there are many people inside those huts, some wounded and some dead," an MSF nurse said.
She said foreign aid workers could not go into the Zairean settlement of Bumba or the camp to reach the casualties because the area was not safe and fighting was still going on.
But MSF relied on Zaireans to volunteer to go into Zaire from Rwanda to the Bumba settlement to bring out the wounded.
One Zairean refugee said he left his wounded brother behind when he fled because he had no means of taking him with him.
"I had to choose between moving my six children out into safety into Rwanda and waiting behind for my brother," said Patrice Mashekere.
Many refugees spoke of Zairean soldiers stealing from them before retreating to Goma city on Saturday.

The Zaireans said former Rwandan troops, who fled to eastern Zaire after the 1994 genocide in Rwanda of up to a million people, were mainly in charge of the Goma area as Zairean troops were badly armed and disciplined.
"It is in a way very nice to be here in Rwanda. At least the soldiers do not steal from us or beat us. Back at home our soldiers behave like animals," said Leonard Banguta, a former schoolteacher.
